newsitem.title: INDIA: India must speed reforms to achieve growth--WTO.
newsitem.headline: India must speed reforms to achieve growth--WTO.

text.p: India must speed its reforms prgramme in order to attain high growth and attract investment, a senior official of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) said on Friday.

"If India is to attain the growth path of seven percent and to receive $10 billion in direct investment...it appears that renewed emphasis needs to be given to the reform programme," WTO deputy director-general Chulsu Kim told an international conference on Asian economies.

"The acceleration of reform would be necessary to overcome the recent slowdown of exports and industrial production, and overcome the serious infrastructure bottleneck faced by Indian companies," Kim told the conference.
He recommended an elimination of quantitative restrictions on consumer goods imports and a further liberalisation of the foreign investment regime.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, who unveiled a market-friendly budget a week ago, said in a newspaper interview on Friday that liberalisation of consumer goods imports would help boost India's "sluggish" import growth and increase customs revenue.
"It is viable and necessary to open up consumer goods imports. Opening up of imports is good in itself. It is an advance on trade policy," he said.
